chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Ibn Ziyad, from Abbas ibn Amir, from Abu Jumaylah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The habitual drinker of wine will meet Allah, Exalted and Glorious, like a worshipper of an idol.'

key_terms.مُدْمِنُ: Habitual drinker / one who frequently consumes

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a habitual wine drinker according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this chain to emphasize that habitual wine consumption constitutes a major sin (*kabirah*) with profound theological weight, equating the drinker’s spiritual state to that of an idolater (*‘abid watathin*). This comparison underscores the transition from mere transgression to a form of practical polytheism, as noted by Shia jurists who view the loss of reason as a precursor to the loss of divine consciousness.
